I got paid today and I've been looking to expand my Wii U library out from last year's releases. I just got Mario Maker yesterday after debating for a week, and I really like it.

I want to know, is the price tag for Splatoon worth it? I have heard there have been a bunch of updates since release, but I don't really know a whole lot about the game as a whole. All I know is that it looks like a shooter that really isn't a shooter. Any downsides for the $60 price tag? It looks fun, but should I wait for a possible discount?

It's worth it. It has a lot of content, and to be honest, the gameplay is really fast and intense. I noticed with a lot of other shooters, you spend a lot of time walking to get to places to find action. In Splatoon, you always have something to do. And if you need to get to the action, you can just quick jump to it.

Being able to paint almost anything and to be able to hide in specific areas adds a lot of game play depth. It lets you do things like set up ganks and flanks in ways you normally can't. Example is I like to hide in a puddle of my ink in a corner most people can't see. Then, they all run past me, and I charge up, kill them from behind, then the team pushes.

The weapons are pretty diverse too. Sloshers are just buckets that lob ink forward. They follow a short range, arced path, which lets you do things like attack over walls. Most of the weapons have pretty different play styles.

The gear too also is a big help, and it does let you play the game differently. One of my favorite builds is to go ninja squid (the enemy can't see you when you're in your ink and swimming) with a short range weapon and then swim up to people and gank them.

My big complaint is the 2 maps on a 4 hour rotation. I try and play at the end of a 4 hour rotation for an hour or two and then get a few hours of different maps. Other than that, though, I really do like the game. It's very fast paced, it reminds me a lot of earlier games like UT2k4/2k3 where you constantly are moving and thinking about what to do, as opposed to games like BF4 where there's a lot of walking or running or driving to get to action.

You do have to get creative and make the most of it. If you play it like a regular shooter you'll probably be disappointed. But if you go into it wanting to take advantage of the mechanics the ink brings, then it's well worth it.
